Chengdu.text: The court is fast and there is altitude, and I like playing in altitude.
After beating Mannarino: “It's a tricky court to play Mannarino on because his ball really slides through the court.”
The balls were really shooting through on this surface, so timing the ball was difficult.
I like this tournament and the conditions suit me pretty well, so it's always nice to be back in Chengdu.
After beating Vacherot: “I like the conditions and feel very comfortable on the court.”
The court here is pretty fast and the bounce is high, which suits my serve and allows me to play aggressively, so I like the conditions.
The conditions suit me well because the balls fly a bit due to us being in the mountains. I played well here last year.
This is my third time in Chengdu, so I enjoy playing here. I love the conditions, the heat and humidity.
First of all, it feels very hot here in Chengdu, but the fans brought amazing energy... The conditions suit me with the fast court and slight altitude.

It was very hot. I couldn't hit a lot of balls because it's very tough to move... Then I was hitting the balls perfectly, but these are very tough conditions. I don't know how many degrees it is now?!
We love it here—the conditions, the people, everything. Playing in China is always exciting, and the fans create a special atmosphere on Centre Court.

Last year when I played, we played Chengdu with Yonex balls, Beijing was Head, Shanghai was Dunlop, then in Stockholm we played Robin Soderling balls, Basel was again Dunlop, and Paris was Head. That really doesn't make sense.

Hangzhou.text: The balls and courts here in Hangzhou are a bit of a flashback to 2019, 2020, 2021. Fast courts. You can serve 205 km/h and aces go through. That's rare on tour now. Here, to come and be able to serve normally, and when you serve well the other guy can't return — it's a great feeling.
It's a fast court, so rallies can finish quickly.

On the conditions suiting him and Rublev: “It seems conditions like these suit us — fast, where you can dictate the game not because you have the strongest forehand in the world, but because you can redirect, play a short cross-court, immediately play into the open corner.”
In America I got broken so many times with those balls.
Because of the balls, the level was just three times higher than everything we saw in the US.
After beating T. Daniel: “It was a really tough match in difficult conditions.”

“It was very fast in America, so I think, on the contrary, the ATP is now working to change the courts. For example, in Hangzhou it was very fast, in Beijing and here – slow, terribly slow.” On his own preference: “I used to hate it, but now, generally speaking, I'm getting the hang of it.”

During the Asian swing I experienced conditions I've never experienced in the past. Hangzhou was actually hotter than Shanghai, but the tournament was smaller so nobody knew about it. It was so hot in the first days, we couldn't believe it. Luckily, they had a roof and it was raining a lot. When conditions are that extreme, we (ATP Tour) have to do what the Grand Slams did—introduce a heat rule or something like that.
It's my first time here and I'm really enjoying my time here so far. It's a little bit hot and humid but this court is really great to play on.

Tokyo.text: “The ball felt bigger and the court slower than indoors. It was frustrating because I couldn't play my usual aggressive style.” On arriving from Laver Cup: “Today it was humid and hot, so the conditions were completely different.”
This [Colosseum] court felt definitely slower than the other court I played on.

I've been here before and like playing here but to be honest, the conditions are so different from the year I won my title here. When I won it was with different balls and it was extremely quick, lightning fast so I loved it. Different conditions but I think it helps being familiar where you are and knowing you've had success here.
After beating Fritz: “It was a tough match with tough conditions. The humidity was tough.”
“Super fast conditions.” (ahead of his match with Altmaier)
“It's pretty quick, we also changed balls from last week, so they were flying a little more here.” (after beating Altmaier)
On the surface and ball differences vs Shanghai: “That's just the way things are when you're out on Tour. You have to adapt week to week.”

The court is obviously playing faster compared to normal hard court events. I'm not complaining about that, to be honest. I think big servers and guys who like to take the ball early and have flat backhands, I think it suits our game style. The court's probably faster than average, but I like it.
It's not easy to play after you win a tournament and come here. Not much time to [adjust] to the court, the balls. Everything is different, so I had to [adjust], which is not that easy.
The courts are playing pretty quickly, so if you're putting a lot of first serves in, I think the percentage to win the point is really high here.

Melzer (Feb 2026) “hard court a touch slower than expected... relatively cold in the hall” = DAVIS CUP indoors in Tokyo, NOT the Japan Open. Fognini and Bagnis quotes = TOKYO OLYMPICS (summer heat), excluded on request.

Beijing.text: The conditions here are super slow. So it's very tough to miss, so you just rally. For whatever reason, at night it plays faster, so I'm waiting for the night matches.
After beating Struff: “The court still feels super slow to me.” On the weather: “It wasn't easy to play in the cold and wind.”
The conditions are a little colder than in the first days of training. The ball slows down a little, the bounce is lower.
After beating Carreno Busta: “The conditions here are very slow, so in a way I think I played even better because I missed less.”
After losing to Djokovic: “It was difficult for me to hit many winners because it was quite cold outside and the ball wasn't bouncing very well.”
After beating Auger-Aliassime: “The last few days it was pretty hot. Today, all of a sudden, it was windy, chilly and cold — kind of a different feeling to play on this court.”
In my opinion, the balls have something to do with it. At the US Open it was really tough to control your shots, whereas here you can control your precision.
After beating Rublev: “It was borderline a hurricane out there. The wind was definitely a big factor.”

On facing De Minaur: “I feel the conditions are quite unique, the court is slow at times especially with used balls. It'll be difficult to get the ball passed him, he is one of the fastest players on the tour.”
After beating De Minaur: “This court is quite slow so he was getting to a lot of balls. It was a very tough match today.”

The conditions are slow so I gave myself a bit of room to return. When the balls are so big and also quite slow, it's tough to be aggressive and almost counterproductive at certain times. I'm still finding out what's the best way forward in terms of tactically on these slower courts.

Said in Shanghai: “It's tough to serve with a heavy ball. In Shanghai and Beijing, both of these tournaments are quite slow, the courts and the ball gets fluffy. But overall I think I found a good rhythm, more placements instead of speed.”
I would say it's not slow and it's not fast. More to the slow side, but nothing like Indian Wells for example.
There were not many winners and a lot of errors, which is normal when it's slow, unless you hit like Carlos or Jannik.
After beating Rublev: “I'm having trouble managing the jet lag, and on top of that, it wasn't easy to play in these very hot conditions.”
I also like the court, with rather high bounces.
I haven't really been here for long enough to feel the conditions. It was muggy, and cloudy, a little cooler.

“I like [the balls] a lot, I feel good. When they open up a bit I play better and have fewer problems than in opposite situations like in New York, for example. I benefit from playing with balls like these from Beijing. You have to be careful about the string tension and other external factors, but in general I feel very good.” Ball: Head

The balls... every week on the calendar, I feel they can't get any slower, but every week I feel they are at least as slow as the previous ones. They become huge, after two games it's almost impossible to hit a winning shot unless you have a very, very fast hand, like Sinner, Alcaraz, or maybe Grigor Dimitrov.
I don't know who is capable of playing aggressively with these balls. They only get bigger and slower. Apart from maybe Sinner and Alcaraz, I don't know who can play aggressively with these balls.
After beating Monfils: “It was a tough match. It's not easy to play here. There was a moment when we were both aware that we couldn't make winners: we ran, ran, and kept the ball in play.”

The conditions really changed, it went from a day match to a night match. It became slower which seemed to suit him as he was able to hit the ball harder and flatter and still keep the ball inside the court.
I feel good on this court. It's a little bit different. It depends how hot it is but tonight it felt like playing indoors and it felt a little slower.
After beating Zverev: “Roof closed, different conditions today, much faster. Both of us are big servers so it came down to just a few opportunities.”
After beating Humbert: “Strange conditions. It was a little bit cold but he missed more than me.”
These balls on this hard court are a joke. You can basically break every game. It's not easy for the mind. I like to play like this, of course, but it's not good for hard-court tennis.
It wasn't the best start. I was struggling a bit with the shade and the sun but I was just trying to fight.

I felt it since the first practice that I did here in Beijing... They change balls in every tournament or almost in every tournament is a different ball... Here in just 1 or 2 games, the ball becomes different from the new ones.
“I always love playing on hard courts but every court is different and I think this one is slower. My serve worked well today and it suits my game well.” (year not confirmed in feed)

Shanghai.text: The court conditions are pretty fast and I like it. Everything is different from Tokyo — humidity, speed of ball and court.

The balls are pretty fast and the court is pretty fast, so the conditions suit me well.
The faster court helps, because at least the ball still moves through a little.
The courts were quite slower [last year] compared to now. Now and then, there was an odd bounce on the court.
I think it's faster than Tokyo. I do feel the speed of the ball here. It does glide a little bit more here than it did in Tokyo. It really benefits aggressive players that go for their shots.
This is a super-fast surface, completely different from Beijing.
The courts here and in Beijing are actually quite similar and both quite fast.
The balls are so fast when they're brand new, but they wear out really quickly. Once they get worn out, it's miserable trying to finish a point.
After beating Kotov: “The conditions were very fast, and I had practised indoors all week.”
“It's a pretty fast court.” Later: “These courts play very fast here so if you serve well it's hard to get broken.”
This court [Stadium] is about three times faster than the other one [Grandstand].
The center court is new, the surface is new, it's faster than last year.
After beating Bublik: “When we play on a surface like this and use that type of balls — with serves that sometimes reach 225 km/h — you don't see many long rallies.”
It feels a little bit slicker on these courts.
Compared to last year the balls aren't as big so that suits my game.
The courts suit me well.
The balls here, which are the same since three weeks, suit me well.
After the roof closed, I felt I could hit with full force and play my game more.
The courts have accelerated considerably compared to last year.
We're still using very heavy balls [Yonex] that are difficult to move.
The balls are exactly the same as those we used in the previous tournament.

It is really different than Tokyo, the ball bounces really slow and I was struggling to get a read on it. I had to play really differently and I didn't have time to play any practice sets. It is incredibly slow here and if I'm being honest the condition change this year is incredibly bad. Last year the courts were obviously fast on the speed index but the balls were slow... now they slowed the courts down, the balls are maybe not as slow but they fluff up very quickly so it's difficult to do anything with them. That's not to mention the humidity, it feels like the ball is going nowhere.

The conditions are tough, very slow. It is very different from what we have been playing. It feels like the slowest conditions I have played in on the circuit. The balls become huge after a couple of games, and the court speed is very, very slow. But there is nothing you can do other than adapt and accept it.

Compared to 2019 the courts are 25 times slower, they're so slow. It reminds me of Indian Wells. I used to hate playing Indian Wells but now I play my best tennis there. It is what it is. It's very slow. I don't think it's the balls, it's the court, it's very, very rough.
The conditions are slow. The heat and humidity have affected matches and led to many withdrawals. You have to be careful, stay hydrated.

It's tough to serve with a heavy ball. In Shanghai and Beijing, both of these tournaments are quite slow, the courts and the ball gets fluffy. But overall I think I found a good rhythm, more placements instead of speed. I'm not the strongest guy ever, so I got to look for the placements and play really smart.

The court and the balls themselves are incredibly slow. The balls are like bowling balls—so big, especially in the evening. After a few games, when they become more worn, it's really difficult to do anything.
It used to be one of the fastest courts on Tour, but now I don't know what is slower, here or Indian Wells. But I've played well on slow hard courts so I hope to keep going.
The lines here in Shanghai are the skiddiest lines ever.
The balls are heavy due to the humidity.

After losing to Vacherot, on the conditions: “It's the same for every player out on the court, but it's brutal.”
I think we should have a rule regarding extreme heat like they have at the Grand Slams, without a doubt... It was around 31 degrees with a lot of humidity — still brutal.
Two days ago it was just absolutely brutal. But the other days are not easy either... You still sweat a lot. I feel really bad for the ball boys and ball girls.
I've got four pairs of shoes because it's one of the few places where I actually sweat through my shoes, and I start making puddles on the court.
No matter the conditions, I can kind of acclimate and get through these long matches.
I always feel good here, the conditions suit me pretty well in China. I was often playing on the other court (Stadium court); I really don't like that court.
Conditions are definitely different than Beijing, so I have only one practice session to get ready.
You would never expect this to happen in a Masters 1000... you can never expect to find a crack on the court in a Masters 1000.

I like most hard courts. But I really like the hard courts where the ball doesn't get destroyed and shredded, and this is a mid-speed hard court that bounces pretty well, and it's usually not too windy.

We are witnessing increased speed on all courts, like at the US Open, where the change from one year to the next was drastic. I consider it important for changes to be more gradual.

What has changed are the balls, which slow the game down a bit more.

I just love playing here, love the conditions, love the support that I get.
I really like the conditions here.
I'm really enjoying the nicer weather in Shanghai.

Wilson balls have a very hard feel and don't have much spin, and the feeling is different every year. They're so heavy I feel like I could play ground golf with them.

I feel at this point, the ball companies are trying to make the worst possible balls and the ATP are doing nothing about it. Beijing, Shanghai and Roland Garros, it's not good enough for professional tennis. They get big. I tried to hit the ball but it just doesn't go from the racquet. Sinner and Alcaraz, guys like that, can generate more power.

The courts are always fast, but you switch balls, the balls are very, like, soft, slow, they can be kind of dead. So I would say the combination of the two makes it like a medium, I would say a medium speed. I think it goes through, especially on the serve.

Almaty.text: It was very difficult to return, especially in these conditions where the court is pretty fast.

“It's very difficult to prepare for the high altitude until you've arrived here... Although there aren't that many meters here, about 800, it's still a challenge. We were here last year, and it wasn't easy — especially returning serve. You just need to get used to it, and that takes time.” On the adjustment: “Sometimes on the first day, you expect it to be hard to feel the ball, and then you actually feel it right away. But the next day... suddenly the ball starts flying away.”

On serving: “It's a mix of everything and for sure the altitude here helps, because you can see in every match that whenever the serve is precise – not even strong – it's tough to return it, so you don't have to go full power, compared to somewhere like Shanghai, for example. For sure when you don't go full power you can gain a higher percentage.”
“Both match courts are excellent.” On indoor tennis: “Indoor tennis is a bit different for us — we don't play much on it back home — but I think a lot of Australians actually enjoy it.”

I was actually shocked by how fast it is this year — I remembered it being quicker than Vienna, but it's even faster than I thought. I like it, though. I'm excited to play in these conditions, and I've always really enjoyed this tournament.

Shanghai was really tough to play in — the conditions were slow and just very different. Unique is probably the best way to describe it, the way everything played there. The conditions here are completely different, and that's a good thing for me.

For me, it brings back good memories — I made the finals here last year. It's a fast court, and I really like playing here. Three really good matches. I like to play indoor and like the conditions here. Today wasn't easy against Reilly as he serves so well.

After beating Diallo: “His serve is unbelievable. I thought I was returning well, but he kept coming up with huge serves — these are good conditions for his game.”

On this surface, of course my serve is a good weapon for me, but I try to be aggressive from the baseline and put some pressure on the opponent. I'm very happy [because it was] a big part of my game this week.
This is a surface I feel comfortable on and my game is coming together.
I think the conditions suit me. It's quite fast and if I hit the forehand well I feel I can get my opponent in trouble.
On moving to Bercy: “I'm going to try to tap a little to see the conditions which will be a little different since they are not the same balls anyway.”

For me, it's a bit slower than the other tournaments. But obviously I had to handle that, I had to work on my problems and change my tactics a little bit in the second set.

Going from clay to hard court is tough and he got in late last night. I expected him to try and make things happen early so I had to hold him off.
He’s a lefty and he is hitting the ball very strong. It was very lively conditions which I think suited him but I like it too.
I knew that dealing with Roman, he’s someone that can play good on this kind of surface. He takes the ball early and pushes you back and that was the main thing that I had to deal with today.
It was a good start. The conditions are different (from Los Cabos), but I feel really very good and happy for this victory.
Here, the court is slow and the ball bounces tremendously, so the rally becomes long and it becomes a physical battle.
The ball bounces tremendously, so the rally becomes long.

I’ve always really loved playing here, but I kind of struggled with the conditions because it’s so hot. But I think I’ve been working really hard on my fitness and also my mental skills in order to cope with the humidity and cope with the suffering of the physical side of it.
The weather is always great, it’s kind of hot and that’s why we play at night. We have the ocean nearby, great food and fans.
It’s not easy conditions here. It’s far from my best or prettiest tennis, but I am staying in the moment.
These conditions are tricky. The opponent was tricky. I’m very happy with the performance.
I liked the conditions since last year, it’s not bad here.

Dubai.text: “Yeah, it’s a bit different from the practice court. It’s a bit slower, a bit more humid. Today the conditions were slower with the ball, so it was tough at the beginning to really find my game.” (match finished around 18:15)
Today the conditions were slower with the ball.

If I get fast courts like this, I can do great things, but there aren’t many courts like this on the circuit. I only remember Brisbane’s court, and I played well there. … When you don’t have to hit the line to get an ace, it’s quite appreciated.
On faster courts like this, where you don’t have to serve on two lines to make an ace, it feels great. It feels like old tennis a little bit.
I can’t complain because we don’t have many fast courts anymore. I think it’s nice to have these kinds of conditions. It’s fast, but I enjoy it, and it’s good to have more specialists.
“On such a fast surface like here, outdoors, it works better.” (of his serve)

What I feel is that all players are hitting the ball harder, and the ball speed is very high. There seems to be an attempt to slow down the pace with the balls and make the conditions slower, but even then, you can tell that the average ball speed is higher than it was years ago.
There seems to be an attempt to slow down the pace with the balls and make the conditions slower.
It’s very different conditions coming from Doha here to Dubai. It’s a lot warmer here, and the conditions are a lot quicker. It’s going to take a little bit getting used to these conditions.

Here is completely different conditions in Dubai. I don’t know if it’s because of the balls or the courts or it’s because of the desert or air. Last week, Doha, and this week, completely different conditions. In my opinion, here is much tougher to play, much tougher to control the ball. I have no idea why because it’s only one hour or even less fly. The weather more or less the same. The balls were the same also I think there.
I think this surface fits well to Bublik. It is fast and it suits his fast shots and drop shots.
I’m feeling good here. It’s a pretty fast court.
In the last game we played, it was ridiculous how slow the balls were. And I don’t understand why the ATP …
It was ridiculous how slow the balls were.
It was a great start, winning the first four games to get a feel for the court. The conditions were a little gusty today, but I got a good early feel for the ball.
Much tougher to control the ball. … The balls were the same also I think there [Doha].
At the beginning, I started a little badly, the conditions were a little different today, there was a lot of wind, it was cold, I had difficulty adapting and I had bad feelings.
The conditions were very tough. The wind was all over the place. At some point I didn’t even know if I had the win in my back or against me.
The conditions is something you never know, so it might not be about me enjoying the conditions here, but just enjoying what comes with the event.
Ball used this week is Dunlop – Australian Open.
I knew in these conditions, really fast and really windy is always tough in the first match. … I like to play with the fast conditions.

I think that this court is playing very quick, actually the quickest I ever experienced the surface here in Dubai. It was always fast, but a lot of players that I talked to have been saying the same thing — it’s very, very fast.
“The surface is extremely fast, especially court 1. I don’t like that, but that is what it is.” (after losing to McDonald)
“Clay, different conditions. He likes the more bouncy conditions.” (on Musetti)

From Doha to Dubai! Since Saturday I have been preparing for my second tournament in the sheikhdom in the desert, the conditions are definitely slightly different: It is hotter in Dubai, the courts are faster as well.
“It’s a fast court and the bounce is high, so I had to step in a little more on return.” (after beating Opelka)
I like the quick courts, they favour my game.
The balls really fly off the racquet.
It’s always special. The conditions are different, there is no roof above, a much faster court, it was hot today, the balls were flying a little more than usual.
“The conditions here are much different from Marseille ... the ball bounces different, the surface is slower.” (coming from indoor Marseille)
The conditions are definitely a bit different because we are now back on the outdoor courts. It’s a bit faster and the ball flying a bit more. I just have to make some adjustments.
Well, I think the wind was even stronger today on the court, changing directions all the time. It was really, really tough to get the rhythm for the serve.

Took me a first few games to really kind of get used to the tricky conditions today. It was pretty windy on the court, even though maybe it doesn’t seem like that from outside. The wind was changing directions all the time. It was completely different from any other day.
The balls were flying a little more than usual.

Indian Wells.text: The courts are quite slow here, so that might suit me. The balls are also quite fast here, so the conditions are a bit slower. On the other hand, the air is a bit thinner here, almost like it’s higher altitude, so the balls fly quite a bit here. The conditions are quite specific here.
Today the ball was tough to control as it came super fast and bounced super high. I just feel really comfortable here. I think this year the court is a little bit faster.

It’s interesting. It’s kind of fast right now. The last few years it’s been slow and gritty, but this year it feels quicker. At night it plays really good. We were kind of in between day and night conditions. The air feels a little warmer, the ball’s moving. I like it.
The balls are also quite fast here … the air is a bit thinner, almost like higher altitude, so the balls fly quite a bit.
The ball was tough to control as it came super fast and bounced super high.

It’s a bit quicker than the last few years, which I prefer. I’ve been pretty vocal about liking quicker courts. It’s still a slow surface, but definitely faster than before. It was windy, but better than the last couple of days. I couldn’t even practice in that wind.

I prefer playing at night here. I’m not even sure I’ve lost at night — the finals are during the day. It’s not that the court is faster at night, but for my game it feels faster. Today the conditions were pretty quick, especially for serve and serve-plus-one. During the day it’s slower and you get more rallies.

“Dunlop in general is slow, and when it wears out it becomes even slower. Lately it’s been wearing out very quickly. I truly believe the quality of the balls has dropped significantly. The issue isn’t the brand itself, it’s the combination of Dunlop and a slow court. The advantage is huge for players who move better.” (ahead of the event)
This court is playing quicker than Indian Wells normally does so that helped me a ton as I was able to rush him a lot.

It’s always tricky here. It’s dry, so the ball flies, but the courts are rough. This year with the ball change I feel like I have more control. During the match the conditions changed a lot — at the beginning it was sunny and the ball was moving more, then after the sun went down I had more control.
With new balls it’s faster. The new Dunlop balls are faster but they also wear out quicker than others. When we’re playing a ball change after a tiebreak — by the way that’s the worst rule in tennis.

The ball just feels so nice for me here. It just keeps finding the court. I’m moving well, and it’s tough to get the ball past anyone on this surface. When it’s hot, the ball jumps, and my backhand stays really low, so it’s all good stuff for me.
The conditions were a bit tricky; they were fast, especially against a player like Marton who plays aggressive tennis and serves very well. It was hard to find my rhythm.
It’s always tough to control the ball with the way he hits it. In these conditions with the wind it was even tougher. I adapted my game a little better than him.
The conditions were difficult as it’s really hot. This tournament is one of the tournaments where we can feel the big difference between day and night sessions.
It’s nice out here to stand back and rip the return because the ball bounces quite high.

The hardest thing was the bounce. The ball jumps really high. If I stand close on the return it jumps over my shoulder, especially on second serves. If I stand far back, it’s not natural for me. I had to find a balance.
It’s tough conditions when you arrive two days before a match, because the ball flies completely differently here.

The wind here is really tough. With the gusts of wind coming in and out and changing directions, it makes it so difficult particularly from one end. It puts extra tension and if you’re tight or not feeling the ball well you’re in big trouble.
This year with the ball change I feel like I have more control.
The ball jumps really high. If I stand close on the return it jumps over my shoulder.

“Penn belongs to Head, and I don’t like Head balls at all. After a few minutes of play, they stop being perfectly round. Sometimes you hit the ball exactly the same, and the result changes depending on the area of the ball you hit. Dunlop balls are not my favorites, but at least they are more round.” (on the Penn to Dunlop switch)
Horrendous day to play tennis. It looks very nice and beautiful with all the people but the weather made it miserable out there, not going to lie. It was difficult on both sides.
Indian Wells will use Dunlop balls this year (formerly Penn).

The court feels the same—very slow with a high bounce. It plays differently at night versus during the day, but when I trained in the heat this morning, the ball was bouncing a lot. I haven’t noticed any difference. They said they changed it, but if nobody had told me, I wouldn’t have noticed.

One thing that I felt was completely different here was the balls. In Dubai, the balls are much heavier. The balls here are a little bit softer and have a lot more air movement than the ones in Dubai. Also, the surface here is rougher on the top layer. It makes the balls bounce a little bit more and not slide around the court as much. I just feel like playing an aggressive topspin game can help here.
I think the conditions help me during the day, the ball is bouncing, it is tough to finish points. It felt slow tonight. It allowed me to stay relaxed and rip the ball.

I find it super slow. It’s probably the slowest court I’ve ever played on in my life. But I’ve played well here before. I started to understand that it was going to be difficult for both of us to hit winners. I realized I just had to run and put the ball in.

I think my serves get good bounces. I get liveliness out of the ball even when it is a little bit colder at night. The conditions are different every week so you have to be able to adapt and adjust. I got here early and put in a lot of work over the last 7 days.

On Center Court, the ball flies, it bounces really high—I don’t think I even played a shot at hip height. I was a bit taken aback by the conditions. I grew up playing on clay, so I’m used to it, but this is unusual for a hard court. It takes time to adjust because the ball-eye coordination has to be recalibrated.

Honestly, the difference between the center court and the others is immense. The ball bounces much higher on the central court than on clay courts. I struggled a lot with that, couldn’t find my rhythm.
The courts are lively, faster than last year.
“I did, and I will be honest with you, it’s okay. I like Indian Wells, I even like the courts now, but they seem to be almost slower than before, very slow.” (asked about the resurfacing)

I don’t notice any difference, but if I had to say something, I would say it’s even slower than before. It’s hard to say this because we know it’s already the slowest on the circuit. It’s slow beyond what the speed index or any parameter says. It’s slow no matter what people say; you can see in the matches how players strive to make a winning shot.

For me, this bounce is normal because I am very used to playing on clay. However, I have to say that the bounce is not normal for a hard court. In Dubai, it didn’t bounce as much, so I had to reconfigure some aspects of my game and adapt. This court is a hard version of clay, indeed.
In Dubai, the balls are much heavier. The balls here are a little bit softer and have a lot more air movement.
Today, it was hotter, and the balls were flying more, which made it harder to control shots and serve effectively.
It was hotter, and the balls were flying more.
Is there a new surface? It seems the same to me, honestly. I trained here for four days, I didn’t notice anything.
They are playing with the same balls. The Penn Tour balls. They fluff up really quickly.

Conditions here this year are very different, I’ve always struggled in years here, but courts are much faster this year, much prefer the conditions. The court is very jumpy, ball jumps very high. I’m a flat hitter of the ball. With my forehand I can use the angles and height to push guys back — with a bit more patience, using the height and allowing the court to do the work for you is important.
The conditions are a little different this year. The balls are definitely quicker and maybe the courts too.
The balls are definitely quicker and maybe the courts too.
Indian Wells ball — Penn.
That’s probably the slowest hard court on the Tour.
Balls get very big and soft after a few games. It used to fly a lot in the desert but that’s not the case anymore.
Always coming into Indian Wells, you feel like the ball flies because of the desert air. But coming from altitude, it’s crazy. I come to Indian Wells and I’m feeling like the ball isn’t moving.

Miami.text: The playing context here feels very different from Indian Wells. The ball bounces much lower and slightly quicker. I've been surprised during practice as I've observed the conditions to be faster than expected, but I think it's due to the heat while being on the court. Each year is different.
It's a court which is quite fast at times, sometimes not depending on how warm it is, but the ball is not bouncing as much. For me that's something I really like.

It's quick. A lot of the courts play differently. I felt like center today played a bit slower than Grand Stand. I feel like Grand Stand is probably the fastest court here. Both of those two courts bounce lower than the practice courts bounce.

The only thing I find annoying about playing on center court is how different it is from the other courts. It will never be the same because it's placed on a football field. It won't be able to replicate the outdoor courts that are laid on asphalt or concrete.
The conditions are probably more suitable for me than in Indian Wells. The courts are much faster. There is more humidity, so the ball stops in the air maybe a bit more than in the desert.
I was hitting hard but they came back almost as quickly. With these slower conditions at night, it's a little more complicated to get the ball past him as he covers the court so well.

It's a bit strange. The court is pretty fast but the balls get old very fast. So at one moment in the rally, you feel like there isn't much you can do, so you can't go for the winner because the risk-reward isn't there. It's the same for the opponent, so we just hit, hit.
It's not easy to play at night, it felt slower and the serve wasn't counting so much, so there were a few breaks.

Conditions are very changeable. At night it is pleasant to play. The wind stops almost completely and the heat is less. But during the day it is much more complicated. Every day that I have played in the morning it has been quite windy and it is difficult to play. The air stops swirling and the conditions are ideal at night.

Bucharest.text: The conditions change a lot, today it was faster but sometimes, like yesterday, it’s cold and slower, but you just have to adapt every day. You can’t control the weather, so it’s about adjusting as best as possible. It’s not easy, but I’m used to these kinds of conditions. In the end, the player who adapts better is the one who wins.
It was a great match in tough conditions. It was cold and rainy, so it wasn’t easy to move. … The break actually helped me. I had been broken twice before, so it gave me a chance to reset.
The conditions were tough and not easy to play in, but I’m really happy to get the win. … Thanks to everyone for coming out and supporting me, even in tough weather.
I really like the conditions here. The courts are in great shape despite the difficult weather, and I enjoy playing here. It’s a place where I feel comfortable and can play good tennis.
I found it a little hard to get into the match — I hadn’t checked the weather and had strung my rackets for yesterday’s conditions. I had to improvise and actually change rackets during the match.
The weather was not good the last two days. … The conditions were pretty slow due to the weather. I like it. I hope it will be the same this afternoon.

“The court should be ok too but it’s not.” (during his match with Moutet, after a couple of rain delays)
Conditions are really tough here. It was just a grinding match, battling match, and I’m just happy to win it in the end.

Houston.text: It was super windy, the court was slick and moving fast and that’s how it is a lot of the time in Houston. It’s actually easier to serve and volley on for me than any other tournament on the calendar.

The clay here, first of all, it bounces up a little bit higher. When it’s pretty sunny, the conditions get pretty fast, so it kind of favors the big servers. In the beginning, it’s a little bit tough to get the footing, it could be a little bit slippery at times, but it’s just a matter of getting used to it.
The clay here bounces up a little bit higher. When it’s pretty sunny, the conditions get pretty fast.
I think the high bounce helps me. The slower the court, the higher the bounce and that means I have more time to create my own power.
It was difficult conditions and very windy. The ball moved everywhere on my ball toss on serve. It was tough but I got the victory. … It’s all about being there mentally and staying patient.
I adapt to clay much faster now than earlier in my career. It was always difficult for me to come to Houston after Miami and switch from hard courts to clay.

After Miami, we took a couple of days in Florida and got a chance to use one of the red clay courts out there. It’s just a matter of getting the footwork down, the sliding, a little bit more strategy out here on the clay because there’s a little bit longer rallies.
I thought it was really difficult conditions with the wind. I served really well at the end of the tiebreak. … It’s my first match of the year on clay and first match in almost a year on the surface.
First match on clay is always going to be difficult and it was tricky conditions with the wind today. I was just trying to find my footing.
It was a really tough match honestly. First match on clay for everybody obviously so I was just trying to get my feet wet a little.
The ball moved everywhere on my ball toss on serve.
This is my fourth year in a row. I love playing here. The clay is different because it’s a different color than Europe, but I like to play here.

Clay is all about footing. You have to be a little smarter with your movement and limit how much you’re changing direction. I had some really long matches here last year, and this court rewards patience if you’re balanced.

It is tough conditions, windy and cold and it is pretty dark. I thought it would be fast during the day, but it was pretty slow at night and cold. There is no sunlight getting into the court so it plays a lot slower.

The courts specifically play a little bit faster than most clay courts, which suits my game. I have a pretty big serve and like fast conditions. This is probably the fastest clay court in the world which suits me.
It is my first time here in Houston. The conditions, I really like it. It is really fast during the day. I feel really good.
Yeah I think the clay is different to South America but at the moment I like it!
We were playing in a tornado and it was challenging conditions at times, but even if I was to lose that I’d have been happy with my performance.
It was tough conditions, first match on the clay, so it was about getting the footing right and it was good to close it out at the end.
It was warmer and the ball was moving a lot more in this match. I’m sweating a bit too.

Marrakech.text: I really like the conditions here. [When] it’s hot and the ball moves fast, it suits my game well and helps me play with confidence.
It’s hot and the ball moves fast.
It’s been a long week here, and the conditions are quite fast, especially coming from the U.S. swing, but I’m really happy to be back on clay. It was very difficult, especially on return.
It wasn’t an easy match, but the conditions were perfect for tennis and I’m happy to get the win. I enjoy coming here and I have good memories from this tournament.
It was not easy conditions, very windy. I am pleased with my performance, a lot better than yesterday.
It was very difficult because of the conditions. The ball was moving all the time. I am very happy to win in two sets.
It was a little difficult to play today in the wind. I tried to keep focused and that was key to the win. Between first set and the break I was focused on myself and not on the conditions.
I am feeling good. I like the conditions here, the court is very hot.
“He likes high bouncing conditions and coming to the net.” (on Herbert)
It was very windy and we both had to adjust. It was tough for both of us to find rhythm at the start of the match.

I feel great in the conditions. It is very good weather for me. It is similar to Granada. I feel I can play my best tennis here.
I love to play here in these conditions. There are a lot of Italians here.

The tournament didn’t start well. I had flight issues so didn’t arrive until Tuesday. Yesterday it was difficult to practice because of the weather. The tournament has done a great job to make the conditions playable.
“He likes the conditions here, he likes the tournament, so I will have to play my best tennis for sure to have a chance to beat him.” (on Andujar)

Monte Carlo.text: The surface is good, the ball bounces and I like it. It’s not extra slow, but it depends a lot on the weather: today it was cool and overcast and the ball was picking up more clay, while in recent days with the sun it was travelling a lot more.

I don’t know the exact degrees but it’s pretty cold. It’s so humid and the balls are so heavy so it’s really hard to hit a winner. I’m really happy about the way I played in the third because I tried to hit a lot harder and be really aggressive whether the conditions were slow or not.

It was my fourth match, and playing against De Minaur in very difficult conditions tonight, I knew I needed a lot more energy. He runs very well and makes very few mistakes.

It’s funny, really. After Indian Wells and Miami, which are quite slow — even though Miami is a little faster — I went back to play on clay… and I swear, I don’t see any difference, except that you slide and the ball bounces higher. There are sometimes bad bounces, the movements are different, but in terms of speed… I would almost say that clay is faster than hard. They’re certainly not much slower.

Today was much slower conditions compared to other days where the sun made it quicker. When I saw it was cloudy today I thought I might be able to do more on return. Shelton was playing very very aggressive so I just tried to return every serve and to stay more calm.
Sometimes the conditions aren’t easy here, sometimes it’s lively and sometimes it’s a bit slower like it was today since we played later.

Physically, it’s harder when it’s cold. You tense up a little more, and when you’re explosive, these conditions aren’t very favorable. You have to find the right balance.
I was trying to find a little bit of purchase off the court, which was a struggle today. It was really tough to get a lot out of the court in these slow conditions.

The conditions are always a bit different. Even though it’s clay. Here it’s actually a bit less slippery than Estoril. The balls are flying differently. It’s not easy. You come a day before the match, you won the tournament but you’re a little bit behind here.

Time. I already have more time to set my footing, to hit big shots. It’s really something that helps me, this notion of time. Every time I give myself time, I can hit big heavy shots and that’s when I’m most dangerous.
The courts are different to Houston last week, where they are much quicker. It’s almost a completely different surface. It was more like a hard court last week.

Obviously clay is not my favorite surface. But I think the conditions have actually suited me this week. It’s not been very warm. The ball stayed low. I’m moving way better on the clay. That’s definitely helped.
It’s not been very warm. The ball stayed low.

Barcelona.text: The conditions were not easy with a lot of wind, so I tried to stay focused and use that. With these conditions, you always have chances because you never know how the ball will bounce. It’s not easy to serve in this weather, so you have to adjust.
“You don’t really realise on TV how heavy and fast his ball is. It took me a set and a half to get used to it.” (on Jodar)
You never know how the ball will bounce.

It started off really hot and there was a big shadow on one side so that made it harder to see. I typically struggle playing in these night conditions but I grabbed a racquet with a little lower tension. I told myself to not make any excuses and play even more physical.
The conditions changed a lot during the match. We started with cold and not much wind, and then it got sunny and hot.

The first thing we have to be grateful for is the sun. The sun was out, it wasn’t raining. There was [however] a lot of wind today, so I had to survive. It wasn’t about playing fantastic tennis, brilliant shots… It was about making the shots you have to do, no more than that.
I felt like I couldn’t find my rhythm and with the conditions, it made it even harder.

I think the court is good. I’ve played on much worse courts than this one, so I’m not complaining. Of course, it’s not Roland Garros – which is the perfect court – but I think it’s almost impossible to reproduce a court like this.
De Minaur is quite good on every surface and the flat shots play well on clay.
The first match was difficult, I came from very different conditions and without rest.
The early sets at the beginning of each tournament are challenging, and adapting to different conditions in such a short time is a bit difficult.
It was a bit of a tricky match—first rounds of tournaments are always like that, and adapting to the conditions is tough.
In general, I am very proud of how I managed to adapt to the conditions. As the tournament went on, I began to play better and better tennis. Now I can say that I am more dangerous on clay too.
The conditions were quite heavy, and I had to really work hard for the points, took a lot of effort out there.
It is a surface where I feel very comfortable, it is the one I like the most. Starting the clay season in this way gives you a lot of confidence.

Madrid is slippery and there is the altitude. These are very particular conditions. Monte Carlo was very fast this year. Here the central court is especially slower; it is quite heavy. But every tournament is different. I like playing here, it’s always nice.
