My shots were heavy, I was able to control most of them. Both forehand and backhand. Patience was there and I knew that was the foundation of today’s match.

“He played very well and his balls are really heavy; some say on the circuit that mine are heavy, but then I advise them to look at the Alcaraz ones — in terms of rotations per minute they travel more or less like the Rafa ones.” (on Alcaraz)
His balls are really heavy … in terms of rotations per minute like the Rafa ones.
Chilly, cold and rainy!! But we through!!
It’s heavy conditions this week. It’s quite cold and the balls are heavy.
It’s quite cold and the balls are heavy.

Munich.text: Here you play at altitude, so it requires different skills. It’s similar to Madrid, where the ball bounces high and moves fast, so I’m trying to build my clay game step by step.
It’s a bit colder, but with the altitude the ball is still flying, so it still makes big servers really tough to play against.
The ball comes very fast, so it’s not easy to control the rhythm. I was really focused the whole match, especially on my serve and being aggressive on the return.
The ball comes very fast, so it’s not easy to control the rhythm.
With the altitude the ball is still flying.
It’s not easy to play here because of the altitude. The ball is flying a lot and it’s tough to control. On the return I was trying to make my ball heavier than his serve, and I think I did that.

“What made me decide to come here is the altitude since I will be playing in Madrid, and the conditions regarding altitude in Munich are similar to what I will have next week.” (on choosing Munich over Barcelona)
It was really tough to come back on a different day with different conditions, but I tried to focus on myself. The court was a bit soft with high bounces, so it made things tricky.

The temperatures don’t really help an aggressive style of tennis. It’s tough to hit winners when it’s like this. We are at altitude, so it helps the servers, but with these temperatures it kind of evens out.
The ball is flying a lot and it’s tough to control.
It wasn’t easy with the cold.

Normally German clay is a bit tricky because it’s very heavy. But here it’s flying through the air more because of the altitude, and I would say clay is my favourite surface. If you gave me one surface to play on, it would be clay — fast clay.

When you get hot weather over here in Europe, the clay plays really fast. But if it’s cold and heavy, you can swing for the fences and it only goes five feet. The weather is so much more of a factor — it affects how the ball flies through the air and comes off the ground.
I am really happy to be here in Munich for the first time. Although it’s a little bit cold, I am feeling really great. I practiced today and yesterday, and I also feel good at the altitude here.
I’m happy to be here again. Last year was a good tournament, I felt like I played well and I like the conditions. I hope the weather stays sunny because otherwise it’s very cold to play.
The entire week has been great. Everyone is enjoying the new centre court — I’m enjoying it myself.

Munich is located just over 500 metres above sea level, which makes the ball fly a little further than usual and that always takes a while to get used to. However, the weather is still quite cool and humid at this time of year, which slows down things a bit, though it’s always good to get used to the conditions as quickly as possible.
The ball flies a little further than usual … but the weather is still quite cool and humid, which slows down things a bit.
Dunlop continues to be the official ball as Munich & Estoril get under way.

Madrid.text: The court is a bit slippery. It is harder to move on it. The ball flies a bit faster. The speed of the game depends on the position of the sun. I practiced on the first day, it was evening, so everything is a bit different. When someone serves very well, it is not easy to return. This is a very unique court. It is very different from Rome and Paris. I think this is a separate tournament on clay courts.

The inside courts are a little bit slower. They have more of a roof, they’re in shade almost the whole day. Outside they’re always with sun. It’s totally different. The outside ones are faster, slippery and smaller. More like faster points, more free points outside than inside. Inside you have to play more rallies.

The way I feel here is that normally with the way the ball bounces in the altitude, the thing that’s under the clay is solid concrete. So whenever whoever plays a good kick serve, you are on the fence actually. The conditions here are more like if you are playing on a hardcourt because you can hold your serve in a much easier way.

It’s definitely a different type of tournament here. I love it. You either love it or hate it, kind of, because there is no in between. Everything is a bit faster, the ball bounces higher, the serve is maybe a bit more effective.
With the altitude, it’s tougher to control the ball and it plays even faster than Munich. Some parts of my game can be really effective here and difficult to deal with.

It’s not so much the clay, but rather the conditions we find ourselves in here; I think it’s the 500-600 metres of altitude that make the difference. For me the conditions suit my game quite well, because I like it when the ball takes the spin I want — here the ball spins a lot and bounces quite high.
It’s a perfect combination — slow clay gives me time, but the altitude makes it faster, which suits my game.

When I’m in the zone, I probably prefer a tiny bit not exactly slower clay courts but not altitude. When I was playing unreal in Rome or Roland Garros, I could play better than here. But here if you serve well you have your chances.

The conditions in Madrid suit me well, there is a little bit of altitude and the ball bounces higher. I am a player who makes the ball bounce quite a lot, and against a player like him that works in my favour.
It’s tougher to control the ball and it plays even faster than Munich.
The Madrid surface? I think it helps my game, it’s a bit faster and it certainly helps my serve too.
I serve really good today. These conditions, fast court — court 4 is a little bit smaller than the stadium. If you serve good it’s really helpful.
I have never played very well here. It’s very particular, you play at altitude. It can be windy, it’s very hard to play. It’s one of the most difficult challenges for me.
Sometimes the court is really bouncy and unpredictable.

If you serve well it’s very effective. You have to play with topspin. If you play flat it might fly on you a little bit. All players that serve well have a better chance of going deep and doing some damage.
You have to play with topspin. If you play flat it might fly on you a little bit.

It bounces very high here, so it’s great for my forehand. I can hit my forehand heavy and spinny, and get it up high on people. I can set myself up and it helps my serve, although it felt like it was really slow tonight (vs F. Cerundolo). It was my first night match but the day conditions are great for me.
Here in Madrid the conditions are somewhat different compared to other tournaments, because we play with altitude, the ball flies and is quite fast. Before I had a hard time finding my level here.

It is an altitude very similar to Chile. It can be a little drier. It is a good surface and good conditions to play. I see the altitude as what it is, I can’t control it and you have to learn to play in these conditions.

“Definitely better. I had more space behind the baseline and perhaps it was even slower than the other courts I have played on so far: there is more gravel on the court.” (on the Caja Magica centre court)

It is my favourite clay court probably. It has an indoor feel even though it’s not fully indoors. It’s got a great sound to it. The court is fast. To me it doesn’t seem like there’s too much clay on the court so, of all the clay courts I play on, it plays closest to a hard court of any of them. The altitude in Madrid just really helps my serve. The ball goes through the air very fast.
The ball goes through the air very fast.

Rome.text: The surface is the same, but the conditions are completely different: first you play in Monte Carlo, at sea level, where the ball bounces quite high and travels a little faster. Munich and Madrid are at altitude, and now we return to a slower clay where you can hit faster and the ball doesn’t go out of control. It’s more like where I usually play.
These are conditions that are very hard for me. The balls stay very heavy all the time, it’s cold, it doesn’t move very fast. I tried to find solutions, I tried to change a few things here and there.
I like the conditions here on the center court: the ball bounces a little higher and travels a little slower — this allows me to really use my backhand the way I like.

I only stepped on the Pietrangeli yesterday, today I’ll train on the Central. We’ll see if the conditions differ depending on the court. It’s slower than Madrid, where the altitude speeds everything up, and more similar to Monte Carlo, at sea level.

The conditions were impossible to play in. The wind was completely crazy. Especially for my game and Alejandro’s, because we both like to hit hard, play fast and dominate the points. When the conditions are like that, that kind of tennis no longer works.
The balls stay very heavy all the time, it’s cold, it doesn’t move very fast.
It was really difficult mentally because we played so late and the court got very slow in the last few games. It was tough both mentally and physically at that time of night.
You can tell that the conditions are very slow because we are coming from playing in Madrid, where everything is faster. It is crucial for me to be sharp with my forehand.

It was very tricky conditions with the wind. When you play with wind, you try to move the ball around a little bit more, and against the wind I’m someone who tries to go quite flat. He’s a big server, so his percentage not being very high helped me.

“You can control a little bit more the rallies because they are going to be always a little bit more rallying when the conditions are slower and a bit heavier. In Madrid, if someone serves very well it gives you a huge impact in a very good way. Here it’s definitely different.” (Rome v Madrid)

It was very windy, and against the wind on clay it’s tough because if you rally too much it becomes difficult to hold your ground. I tried to make the points shorter on that side. With the wind behind my back, I tried to play as heavy as I could.
Playing a player with such a huge serve like Jiri has and aggressive play, it’s not too bad to have a little bit of extra time and the conditions being a bit slower.
I tried to use the slower clay here to my advantage after Madrid and was really happy with how it worked out.

I like the court because in Rome every court feels a little bit different, and the center court is not too fast and not too slow. It’s kind of medium speed. If I’m not wrong, I still haven’t lost on center court. I lost on the grandstand.
It was very tough conditions with the wind. I don’t think either of us played our best tennis today because the conditions were difficult, so I just tried to adapt in the best possible way.
It was super tough to even play tennis with the wind — the ball was moving all the time.

Here every year it’s kind of very heavy, especially on a day like today which was also raining, cloudy, the humidity you could feel it in the air. It’s much more difficult to just get advantage with a serve and then with a shot. You cannot just make one easy winner from the baseline.
The final was difficult, with the schedule and so much sun and shade. For an hour it wasn’t easy. And the wind was changing, it was hard to play good tennis.
The ball was moving all the time.
Every year it’s kind of very heavy … you cannot just make one easy winner from the baseline.
It’s slow conditions here, especially coming from Madrid. But the sun came out and that helped. I felt like the Centre Court is maybe a little faster than the other courts.
It’s quite a slow court so I was surprised to see 16 aces on the board. I wasn’t happy with the rain at the start as it makes it a lot slower, but then the sun came.
The conditions here are significantly slower than in Madrid; I think all players would tell you the same. Even though we say this is standard clay, Madrid’s surface is more unusual.
“It seemed slightly faster than Pietrangeli but not too different overall. I had a good time.” (on the SuperTennis Arena)

Two years ago, there were bad bounces here, but I managed to catch some confidence, and due to this, win the tournament. And maybe in Madrid, on a good, ideal court, in ideal conditions, some clay court player would have beaten me.
I’m very pleased, especially coming from Madrid to here. It’s not always not easy because Madrid is at altitude and the balls are flying like crazy, but here everything is pretty slow.
Madrid is at altitude and the balls are flying like crazy, but here everything is pretty slow.
Of course I need to do some things on my game, try to push harder because conditions are really slow. These kind of conditions are tough for everyone.
Each court has different conditions: the Central is slower, the Grand Stand is faster especially in the afternoon.

Geneva.text: The courts are playing pretty quickly. The altitude helps, there’s not a ton of clay on the court, and with the new balls they’re really moving.
“The balls aren’t the same, and there’s a bit of altitude here.” (comparing to Rome)
With the new balls they’re really moving.
The balls aren’t the same [as Rome].
It was very cold and obviously tough conditions so I wasn’t really feeling the ball at the beginning. But I managed to play some tough tennis.

It was difficult conditions — the ball was bouncing a lot. I stepped up and pushed through. I never played here before, so it was tough at the start. Like I said, the ball was bouncing a lot, so I had to adjust.
The ball was bouncing a lot, so I had to adjust.
The conditions were tough this week.
“Reilly with the serve and the altitude, it is tough to return his serve.” (on facing Opelka)

Hertogenbosch.text: In the first match you're never quite sure what to expect. It's my first time playing on this court, so there are a lot of adjustments to make. You have to pay attention to how you move, how the ball is bouncing and how the court is playing.
That's grass-court tennis. Matches like this happen a lot on this surface because it's not easy to get breaks of serve. A lot comes down to serving.
It was a very tricky match against a tricky opponent in tricky conditions. There wasn't a lot of topspin being played today so that made for some interesting rallies.
Everything was a challenge today. There was a bit of wind, a bit of rain and a very good, very tricky opponent on the other side of the net.
During the first week you never really expect anything special because grass is such a unique part of the season. The transition from clay to grass is always tricky.
It has been a good serving week, especially when it is a hot day today. In conditions like this the ball reacts more to the different spins I produce on my serve so today was good serving conditions.

The weather was horrible, it just rained. At one point, I arrived on the court and, after two minutes, it was raining: they had closed the training courts. I played a lot on indoor hard courts and maybe three hours on grass before starting my first match.
Rough conditions the last few days but that's what we expect at this part of the season. A lot of start, stop.
The transition from clay to grass is always difficult. That's why it's great to play in 's-Hertogenbosch. I try to be aggressive and often return serves from deep, even on grass.

I came early and felt good with my preparation. I prefer these faster courts. To switch from clay to grass gives me a nice feeling, even if you have to take some time to get used to how the surface plays. It brings with it quite a bit of muscle pain in the first few days because you suddenly feel so much lower to the ground.
You have to adjust a bit in terms of movement and shorten your back swing a bit, but that suits me. Even then you have to sit low and get to the ball quickly.
It was super tricky, super windy.
It was pretty tough. I never felt comfortable for a moment. It was mainly very hard work. In the first 2.5 sets he deserved to win the match but the rain came and that suited me very well.
The biggest challenge was to adapt on grass as I didn't play too many times on grass, and also with these conditions it was very difficult.

Roland Garros.text: The heat is changing the conditions of the tournament enormously. We have never had a Roland Garros this hot in May. On court 14 the conditions were especially fast: the ball was moving a lot, bouncing very high, and on top of that the balls are quite hard. Clearly there are players who benefit much more than others from these conditions.

The heat changes the playing conditions more than the physical aspect. It’s never been this hot at Roland Garros. The conditions on Court 14 were really rough. The game is pretty fast on the angles, the ball bounces a lot.

Today, the conditions were extremely fast, incredibly difficult to control the ball. These are conditions where it’s really difficult to play a very aggressive style of tennis because it’s so hot. First, you have to be able to hold on, and then you mustn’t lose control of the ball because it bounces around a lot.

The conditions here are actually pretty fast. In the past I often played in very cold conditions in Paris where the ball didn’t travel much, but this time the ball is bouncing much higher, so it feels completely different.

When I was just starting out, the courts in Paris were exactly like in Madrid — it was concrete you could slide on, and I really enjoyed it because there’s no altitude and the ball bounces lower. Probably over the last three or four years it has completely changed.

The conditions are a little different every year. At the start they were slower, now they are starting to speed up. But it is still clay tennis. The rallies are longer and slower. It is also a lot about physical readiness. I like playing in the heat.

The organizers water the court so much in the evening, in anticipation of the heat the next day, that I actually found it quite muddy. The entire beginning of the match was quite heavy and damp. The balls were covered in dirt, wet. If they didn’t water it so much, it would be like a beach all day long.
I think they’re right, most Americans like slightly faster conditions. Anytime I can improve my timing, it helps me.
The ball was moving a lot, bouncing very high, and the balls are quite hard.
The balls were covered in dirt, wet.

Conditions will be different this year. In the evenings it can usually get quite cold here, with rain and some strange weather in recent years, but now it is over 30 degrees in the first week. You have to try to familiarise yourself with that type of situation.
I love playing on courts like Chatrier. I have great memories here. It’s perfectly normal that when you’re not very high in the rankings, you’re placed on smaller courts, which you’re less used to.

“The ball bounces higher, but this court is, in any case, slower than Chatrier and Suzanne Lenglen. So, I think it’s a different court. I had to find my rhythm a little at the beginning. Today, there was no wind, there were no gusts. Yesterday, it was windier; so, it was different to play.” (on Simonne Mathieu)

The players at Roland Garros switch to Wilson balls after playing the clay season with Dunlop. Dunlop: heavier, fluff up faster, slightly softer. Wilson: longer lasting (more durable), lighter, fly faster through the air, more consistent bounce.

These courts are really fast. Whoever shoots first to the side can have a big advantage. So it’s often about who will dictate. Of course with this weather the ball was much slower today, but generally, these courts can be fast, which is not normal for a clay court.

Yes, quite fast, especially with new balls, Roland Garros has always been like that. I like the courts with lots of space, there is more space to defend and counterattack, which is in my repertoire. But it also went well today in a narrower court (C12).
It was sunny and hot. So it’s really fast and it bounces really high, which is good for me and my game.
Quite fast, especially with new balls.

The weather conditions we have had this year are quite unusual. There was a lot of rain, very wet, muddy, really heavy conditions that affected the court, the humidity and everything else, and that affected the surface which is a living surface, like grass. The clay is a surface on which we can intervene in some way with a little work and care of the land.
I cannot say 100% if it’s the balls, the surface... but from what I heard from all the players, everybody agrees that it’s, let’s call it slower this year, and the balls get big.
Everybody agrees that it’s slower this year, and the balls get big.

Yeah, it’s getting very, very slow, the ball. It’s getting very fluffy and big. It’s making the game very slow. It’s not my favourite ball, to be honest. For sure the ball is slower and it feels different compared to last year.
It’s getting very fluffy and big. It’s making the game very slow.
The balls are much heavier, so I’m sure it’s going to be much more rallies than previous years. They felt really heavy for whatever reason.
The balls are much heavier … they felt really heavy for whatever reason.
Here at Roland Garros it depends a lot on the weather, with sun it is very fast and when it is cloudy it is super slow. I like it cloudy and the conditions are more like normal clay courts.

Sometimes people still think clay is slow. It’s not that slow. If you’re playing on a day when it’s quite warm then it can be faster than most hard courts… unless you go to Cincinnati and Shanghai and a couple of indoor events.
The conditions are very fast and much faster than other hard courts.
These balls during the day are bouncing really high.
These balls during the day are bouncing really high.
Clay in Roland Garros feels great this year. Especially Wilson balls. Said it from the beginning. To beat me, now guys have to play well.
Especially Wilson balls.
So far I have been playing amazing. I didn’t feel that it was clay. I felt like I was playing like on hard courts. I really like the conditions here so far.

“The balls are very good! They have a lot of felt on the ball and remain consistent. The wear and tear is not too bad but if the ball or court is wet it does impact the flight. I expect that the colder temperature and humidity will also impact the bounce. It’s not as lively as before.” (coach)

This is the first time that we are using Wilson balls on the clay. I agree that the balls are heavy. But also it’s probably because we are almost in October and it’s very cold. The clay is also heavy and wet. It’s hard to say whether the ball is heavy in general or is it because we are playing under these slow and heavy conditions?
I agree that the balls are heavy … the clay is also heavy and wet.

The balls are going to be, without a doubt, the biggest difference. The Babolat were my favourite balls, they were comfortable and quite fast, perfect for my game as well as for Nadal’s. The new balls are a bit slower. Of course that this will change the results a bit.
“It’s not the right balls to play on clay courts. The organization needs to take a look at this in the future — it’s dangerous for elbows and shoulders of the players.” (on the ball change)

Some of those balls we were using you wouldn’t give to a dog to chew. It’s brutal. It’s so cold. I think the balls are the biggest thing. Maybe they got it a little wrong with the balls. It’s tough to get that ball to go anywhere. That ball’s a bit too heavy.
The balls now are way better than before. The Babolat balls were the worst of all time.

London.text: The courts here are notoriously low. The grass is cut very short, which makes them play quicker and allows the ball to skid through the court. When it's warm, everything plays a little bit quicker. The wind makes it quite difficult because the ball doesn't bounce very high, so you have to be very sharp with your footwork.
It feels like the grass here is a bit shorter, so the ball bounces a little higher. Usually at Wimbledon the surface is a bit slower and the bounce is lower – sometimes the ball kind of gets stuck.

The bounce here is much lower, the surface is very fast, so many rallies are completed quite quickly. When playing on grass, my height creates additional difficulties, because it is more difficult for me to work with balls that remain low above the court.
The ball stays quite low, and it's quite a fast surface.
It's so good for my style of game. It makes the things that I do really effective. You get rewarded for coming to the net on grass.
I do prefer the court being worn in a bit. I know at Wimbledon I always like it in the second week. The courts here are feeling really great.
My style of play has always suited this surface well. The pace is a little higher, the ball comes at you faster. I try to take the lead quickly in the point, whether on serve or return.
I was happy to get on a faster surface to be honest.

Adjusting to grass for me is not that hard because it fits my style. The surface helps my game be even more effective. It's great to be back here at Queen's, some of the best grass courts in the world.
I had one racquet in my bag which was a bit of a higher tension. There had been quite a lot of points during the match where the ball just flew off my racquet a little bit.
Grass is a walking MCL sprain!
The courts are terrible – the court is too wet. It was same on both sides. He managed to not slip. I just need to get better balance for the upcoming tournaments.
The first practice I have done here, my movement wasn't as good as last year but it is a slow process, so I have to be really focused in every practice and every match.
I step on a grass court and I feel like I've just gone into my living room at home. It feels that comfortable, I feel so natural. Going back onto the grass is really natural.
Grass is so much faster than clay so if you are late to the ball there is a lot of pressure on the wrist.

The most difficult part of playing on grass is being able to move well. You have to be more careful than on the other surfaces. There are a lot of players who slide on grass and I'm not one of them, so I have to think a lot more about my movement. It can be more tiring because you're constantly moving – it's totally different to the other surfaces.
Every match I'm playing I feel like I'm playing for ten years on grass. My movement and my game I did not expect to improve so fast on grass.
I think the most important is that I came with a very, very humble approach to the surface and was ready to adjust it at any moment. We all know how tough it is to move on grass.

It was very tricky conditions, I wasn't able to get my usual patterns or hits, so I had to change it up a little. I served well when I had to. All in all very happy with the match but difficult conditions for sure.
It doesn't get easier when the courts are this good. Definitely the best grass courts I've ever played on and it's easy to get comfortable.
The conditions were much different than yesterday, it was hot and I had to drink a lot of water but today I preferred it. There was wind of course but it was cooler.
That was really tough. The conditions were hot, windy.
The guy who keeps his head in the conditions is the one who wins because the conditions were difficult. It is important to move well and to serve well.

When you play the first match, it's always tough, because the grass is slippery and you have to be physically so strong. To play on grass, you have to be focused on every point because it can escape, the games, so quickly.
First day on the grass as it is a little bit slippery. I am pleased I was able to apply constant pressure.
That first match on grass is never easy. The courts tend to be very green and quick, and it's quite difficult to move on.
The conditions was very different to the last couple days. Credit to him he was serving big, but the slower conditions definitely suited me a little bit more. The court was slippery towards the end.
We only got three hours of practice time on the grass before the first match, but we missed the grass last year.

Mallorca.text: The grass is a bit drier, with irregular bounces due to the weather. In London it rains a lot, here it seems to wear down more easily, the conditions are a bit slower. The conditions are made for suffering because it's very hot.
As the courts slow down, I feel like I can take bigger cuts at the ball.

The conditions are pretty specific. The grass is bouncing a little higher and with the heat you want to keep the rallies short. The grass helps with that. It's not like clay or hard courts where you have to survive through long rallies. The return is especially important here because of the conditions. You have to serve well and return well. That's even more important here than at some other tournaments.
It's a little slower than some of the other grass courts I've played on this year, which is a good change. I felt really good.
As the match goes on, the balls get bigger and it becomes a little easier to return big serves. I knew it was going to be hot. Summer in Spain is always very hot, so I expected a tough battle.

The conditions were completely different here compared to Halle. It was much hotter and the courts played very differently. Because of the heat, you have to make some adjustments. Every court is different as well, so you have to adapt.
It was very hot today, but at least it was on grass, so the rallies weren't too long. I actually prefer it this way rather than when it's too cold.

With these conditions and this weather it was very difficult. It was so hot today and it was tough to find the energy to compete for every point. I tried to be aggressive with both my serve and my return because on grass you need to finish points in two or three shots. That's the key to playing well here.
It's different playing here in Mallorca as it's very hot. But this is my first match on grass so this one is more difficult. The serve was a key and the mental moments were tough.
It's still grass, so you have to be ready and react very quickly to those serves.
I love the heat. The warmer, the better for me. I really enjoy playing at this time of day.
It's definitely a little nicer when the sun goes down. We knew it was going to be hot here in Mallorca, but you have to adapt either way.
It was super hot again today. And when you're nervous, it feels twice as hot. Respect also to the audience and the ball kids for holding up so well in this heat.
It took a bit to adjust to the heat at first, but today the conditions were much better.

It's quite hot but I feel I'm quite used to it. There's a bit of breeze so it's not bad. Grass is a tricky surface. After all these years I am becoming more and more comfortable on it, but it's not something that comes naturally to me.

It's been really hot in Mallorca for sure. I thought it might be a bit cooler at night but the temperature didn't really change and I had to deal with it. I think I settled in pretty quickly with the heat and it wasn't too bad.
I'm getting used to the grass, day by day. Happy with the weather here.
It was really fun to play. The conditions were great. We both served well. The shots feel good, I feel good. The only thing missing is rhythm from play and maybe the reaction on return.
The courts suit my game here. I almost beat Eubanks last year and he went on to win the tournament. There are not many places on Tour like this.

The playing conditions are really not good. The surface is really very bad, to put it mildly, it's just about managing it all the time. Suddenly, it is difficult to engage in strikes due to all the bad bounces.
There's bad bounces on court, but I feel I'm able to handle that better than most players.
The grass is faster than in Germany, and the bounce is also higher.
It feels I'm playing longer matches on grass than on clay.

The weather is perfect. That's the most important thing. In London it is raining every day. If you want to practice a lot on grass here the conditions are perfect. It's very good preparation for Wimbledon.
The weather was great, the tournament is amazing, the grass is good. Everything is perfect in Mallorca.
“I wish the court was a little cleaner,” referring to the amount of sand on the court.
In general the most important shot on grass is the serve. If you can make a few returns you can benefit from that.

Halle.text: On a court like this, you get some dodgy bounces, especially later in the week when the court gets torn up. You have to be careful with the balls you take early, take a lot of extra little steps and try to take the ball out of the air as much as possible.
The ball stays quite low, and it's quite a fast surface.

It's very tough to break serve on grass in general, but when it's 32 degrees and we're all serving above 140 miles per hour, it's even tougher. The court has already taken some damage throughout the week, which makes it even harder to break. The conditions suit the big servers quite well, and that's why the results have been the way they are.

Grass gets tricky as there's a ton of on and off bad bounces. It's tough to play against me with that because my backhand stays low and I'm in a good serving rhythm. I'm also moving great as you can move really nicely here.
